headline: High: Prefect can egress broadly while Botpress lacks isolation details, creating default-path leakage and workflow-conflict risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented shared channel to Prefect, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Prefect can consume workflow metadata and call APIs, so if Botpress output is manually or operationally fed into Prefect, prompt-like content could be misused. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into Prefect task inputs or workflow metadata
IF Prefect parses Botpress-generated text as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Add a strict text-to-parameter schema before Prefect ingestion
Strip instruction-like markup from Botpress outputs
Require human review for any Botpress-to-Prefect handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has network egress none, while Prefect has broad egress and touches workflow metadata. If they share a workspace or Botpress outputs are routed into Prefect, sensitive content could leave the local boundary through Prefect’s outbound connectivity. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs contain sensitive workflow content
IF Prefect is configured to transmit those outputs to external services or APIs
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Prefect on separate workspaces
Disable outbound connectors for Prefect jobs handling Botpress output
Redact sensitive fields before any Prefect handoff
Log and review all Prefect egress destinations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Prefect has broad network egress plus API-calling behavior. Even without explicit filesystem write fields, both can mutate shared operational state through packages, workflows, or API-driven side effects. Because write surfaces are not fully documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same deployment or package environment
IF Prefect tasks and Botpress runtime modify shared artifacts or dependencies
mitigations: Run each agent in separate containers or environments
Freeze deployment changes during concurrent runs
Add a simple ownership rule for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate customer-support content, and Prefect is an orchestration tool that may act on workflow metadata. If Prefect treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream automation. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium, not low.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Botpress output as an input to automated tasks
IF no validation or approval step checks Botpress-generated claims
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Prefect actions
Require human approval for Botpress-derived decisions
Limit Prefect actions to read-only dry runs first

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress and Prefect are both open-source with no documented residency or certification mismatch in the profiles. Prefect touches workflow metadata, but there is no evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border handling. Because the compliance pathway is undocumented and narrow, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent’s workflows
IF deployment policies require specific residency or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Review deployment region and logging defaults
